source.title: Corrupting Neuron Explanations of Deep Visual Features
source.authors: Divyansh Srivastava; Tuomas P. Oikarinen; T. Weng

page_placements.theme: Interpretability scores and explanations can be inflated, manipulated or unreliable

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether probing-data corruption changes visual-neuron explanations, but does not test any of the listed versions about job shares, explanatory prediction on new activations, or language-model neurons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on corrupted probing data changing neuron concepts or descriptions. These bear on neuron-explanation reliability generally, but do not measure any of the listed claim versions. The paper also reports validation accuracy under corruption and comparisons among corruption methods; those results do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study attacks visual-CNN neuron explanation methods (Network Dissection, MILAN) by corrupting probing data. It reports how often assigned concepts change. It does not measure the share of neurons with one job, does not check explanations by predicting activations on new inputs, and does not study language models or attribution graphs. Its results concern how robust explanation pipelines are, not whether neurons are clean, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that neuron explanation methods are not robust to probing-data corruption. Gaussian noise of std 0.02 changes concepts for up to 28% of deeper-layer neurons. Their designed corruption manipulates over 80% of neurons while poisoning under 10% of probing data. Higher-layer units with higher-level concepts are easier to manipulate.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates visual CNN neuron-explanation methods (Network Dissection and MILAN) under probing-data corruption; it does not use the original language-model pole-audit method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported manipulation rates vary with model, layer, perturbation magnitude, corruption type, and targeted versus untargeted setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Designed probing-data corruption changed Network Dissection concepts for up to ~96–100% of units in higher layers of VGG16-Places365 and Resnet50-Imagenet at ϵ=4–6/255, with targeted success up to ~57%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron concept labels from probing-based explanation methods for vision CNNs can be manipulated by small, imperceptible perturbations to the probing dataset, more easily in higher layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Gaussian noise (std 0.02) lowered MILAN description similarity, to mean F1-BERT ~0.83 in conv4_3 and conv5_3 of VGG16-Places365.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random noise in probing images alters MILAN neuron descriptions, more in deeper layers.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The reported outcomes concern changes in explanation assignments/descriptions under probing-data corruption, not how accurately explanations predict neuron firing on new examples or the share of neurons with one or more jobs. Some results use F1-BERT similarity as a proxy for semantic change.
record.rows_left_out: The 53-row selection includes all Table 2 Network Dissection conditions and Table 1 MILAN Gaussian-noise results at standard deviation 0.02. Other noise magnitudes, MILAN designed-corruption results (including Table 3 and Appendix Table A.7), bounded-noise results (Appendix Tables A.2-A.3), corruption-category results (Figure 4), accuracy results (Figure 5), and comparisons in Figure 6 and Appendix Tables A.5-A.6 are not extracted.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job shares.
No language models, scale sweep, or dense/MoE comparison.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis, pose feature, or superposition test.
No estimate of interpretable-neuron share, nor its dependence on architecture, regularization or tools. The adversarial-training result concerns attack robustness, not interpretability share.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No test of whether activating-example explanations predict firing on held-out inputs.
No simulation-based scoring of explanations on new text.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source and tests no version. It is tangentially related to reliability of neuron explanations (cf. V6), but it measures sensitivity of explanations to corrupted inputs, not their predictive accuracy. Relation 'discusses' is generous: the paper does not engage the claim directly.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimates of single-job, two-job, or not-understood neuron poles.
No language-model comparison, model-scale sweep, or dense/MoE comparison.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis or test of pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
The study uses visual models but does not estimate their interpretable-neuron share or test architecture, regularization, tool quality, or the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution-graph test or comparison with replacement models and reconstruction error.
The study corrupts probing data; it does not test whether explanations derived from activating examples predict firing on new inputs.
No automated scoring of explanations by simulated activations on new text or minority-good-score result.

relation.reason: It fits. The study is about neuron explanation methods, but it tests no version.

tranche.reason: It attacks the robustness of neuron-explanation methods for visual CNNs. It does not measure the share of interpretable neurons or whether explanations predict activations, so it neither tests nor uses any version.

source_check.notes: Only R01-R25 of 53 rows were in the pack. Table 2 is flattened but its cells place consistently. VGG16 higher-layer untargeted: 95.74-100%. ResNet50 layer3/4: 98.63%. The targeted maximum is 56.86% (VGG16 conv5_3, eps=6/255). The ResNet50 targeted maximum is 46.05%.
